item.title: 「日本復活」は本物か、ブルームバーグのアンカーが円安と物価高の現場を歩いた
item.description: 1ドル190円も現実味？「日本復活」の行方をインタビューから読み解く。

item.title: EQT Agrees to Acquire Australian Smart Parking Tech Firm Orikan
item.description: EQT AB agreed to acquire Australia’s Orikan, saying it will help the smart parking technology company invest in innovation, strengthen its business and expand into adjacent markets.

item.title: Israel Set to Cut Rates on Strong Shekel and Enduring Ceasefire
item.description: Israel’s central bank is set to cut interest rates for a second straight meeting as a strong currency and moderate inflation expectations outweigh an anticipated pickup in growth and shift toward more restrictive policy in the US and Europe.

item.title: China’s Biggest ETF Is Now a Gold Fund as National Team Retreats
item.description: A China spot gold ETF has overtaken the Huatai-PineBridge CSI 300 ETF to become the country’s largest exchange-traded fund, highlighting the extent to which state-backed support for the stock market has faded.

item.title: Corn Jumps as French Crops Damaged by Intense European Heat Wave
item.description: Corn futures surged after a heat wave damaged crops in France, one of the European Union’s biggest producers of the grain.

item.title: Ather Energy Is Said to Plan $200 Million India Share Sale
item.description: Ather Energy Ltd. is planning a share sale to institutional investors as early as next week to raise as much as $200 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Iron Ore Rises on Fortescue Curbs and as Slump Spurs Buying
item.description: Iron ore rose after China’s state-backed buyer of the commodity expanded curbs on Australian miner Fortescue Ltd., and as a slump in prices over the last couple of months attracted buyers.

item.title: Thai Inflation Cools Again, Reinforcing Central Bank’s Rate Hold
item.description: Thailand’s headline inflation slowed for a second straight month in June even as underlying price pressures continued to build, reinforcing the central bank’s view that the recent pickup in prices unlikely warrants an immediate interest-rate increase.

item.title: Asia Pacific Private Credit Growth to Slow, Moody’s Ratings Says
item.description: Growth in private credit fundraising and deployment in the Asia Pacific will slow over the next 12 to 18 months as macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and elevated interest rates weigh on investor appetite for illiquid assets, according to Moody’s Ratings.

item.title: Copper and Aluminum Advance on Fading Expectations for Rate Hike
item.description: Copper rose for a third day and aluminum extended a rebound from a four-month low, supported by fading expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

item.title: Unease Over Korea Leveraged ETFs Grows as Lawmakers Demand Fix
item.description: South Korean lawmakers are increasingly sounding alarms over the risks of single‑stock leveraged exchange‑traded funds, with an opposition party member now calling for such products to be delisted.

item.title: ByteDance, Alibaba Pull AI Companions as Beijing Tightens Rules
item.description: ByteDance Ltd. and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. are pulling the plug on features that let users build and chat with AI companions, preparing for new Chinese regulations governing human interactions with artificial intelligence.

item.title: India Stocks Shine as Foreigners Seek Defense Against AI Storm
item.description: A stronger macro backdrop and optimism ahead of the earnings season are adding to the appeal.

item.title: Goldman Cuts Yen Forecast to 165 Per Dollar, Likes Carry Trades
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. sees the yen weakening to 165 per dollar in a year’s time, driven in part by Japan’s interest rate differentials with the US.

item.title: Pakistan Buys More LNG as Flows Through Hormuz Fail to Recover
item.description: Pakistan bought a liquefied natural gas shipment for delivery later this week, as exports from main supplier Qatar through the Strait of Hormuz remain constrained.

item.title: US Beef Exports to China to Pick Up as Rivals Exhaust Quotas
item.description: China’s decision to renew import licenses for hundreds of US meat plants is yet to revive the beef trade, but the odds of more shipments in the second half of the year are improving.

item.title: Weaker Commodity Prices Set to Tip Australia Into Trade Deficit
item.description: The boost to Australia’s trade from the mining boom looks to be fading as imports soar and export growth flatlines, potentially putting it on track for the first annual deficit since 2016.

item.title: Self-Driving Startup Turing Gets AMD Backing, Adopts AMD GPUs
item.description: Self-driving tech developer Turing Inc. has added AMD Ventures to its list of backers and begun adopting Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI accelerators in its systems.

item.title: India Banks Slash Short-Term Debt Sales on Cheaper Forex Funding
item.description: Indian lenders are pulling back short-term debt sales as the central bank’s recent push to attract foreign-currency deposits has opened up a cheaper and more durable source of funding.

item.title: Ringgit May Rebound on Capital Flow Measures, Analysts Say
item.description: The ringgit is poised for a rebound after ending June as Asia’s worst performer, with measures to boost foreign-exchange inflows and strong economic fundamentals expected to support the recovery, analysts say.

item.title: Bankers Say Asia Loan Market to Stay Weak as War Saps Confidence
item.description: Asia’s loan market is heading into the second half of the year with little sign of a rebound, according to bankers, as the fallout from the Iran war continues to suppress confidence among lenders and borrowers.

item.title: Chip Stock Bulls Count on Samsung to Soothe AI Trade Jitters
item.description: A wild ride for global chip stocks in recent weeks has left investors looking for fresh validation of the artificial intelligence trade. Samsung Electronics Co. may provide just that on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold Steadies After Weekly Gain as Rate-Hike Worries Recede
item.description: Gold steadied after posting its first weekly advance since May, supported by reduced expectations that the US Federal Reserve will hike interest rates.

item.title: UK to Toughen Up Political Donation Rules in Latest Crackdown
item.description: Political donors will need to wait a year after returning to the UK before they can give more than £100,000 ($133,510) as part of a proposed crackdown on offshore political finance that threatens to hit Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.

item.title: Burnham Adviser Urges Next PM to Consider Radical Tax Overhaul
item.description: A group of economists including Andy Burnham adviser Jim O’Neill have called for a wide-ranging overhaul to turbocharge Britain’s sluggish economy, with the former Greater Manchester mayor set to take another step toward Downing Street later this week.

item.title: CATL Invests in New Zealand Firm to Develop Graphite From Wood
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. is investing in a New Zealand-headquartered company that converts forestry byproducts into graphite for use in lithium batteries.

item.title: Sara Duterte Faces Impeachment Trial With Philippine Presidential Dream At Stake
item.description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte faces a contentious trial in the Senate from Monday, a case that could end her political career or leave her as the top contender to succeed archrival Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as president.

item.title: Trump’s War Means Higher Global Interest Rates for Years to Come
item.description: Donald Trump’s war against Iran may be over, but the repercussions for global monetary policy are here to stay.

item.title: Genesis Makes Rival Bid for Vault in $3.9 Billion Deal
item.description: Australian gold miner Genesis Minerals Ltd. has launched a last-minute cash and stock bid for Vault Minerals Ltd. which had already agreed to a deal with Regis Resources Ltd.

item.title: Oil Slips on Hormuz, US Stock Futures Hold Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil edged lower as energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz persisted and OPEC+ signaled higher supplies. Traders were also focused on the Korean won’s first day of 24-hour trading.
